messages.subject: p-x-k matrix?
parts:
Hello everyone,
I am sure this is a simple fix but I am very new to R so please bear with me. I am trying to but 30 equidistant two-dimensional semilandmarks along a closed curve but I keep getting an error code 


Error in digit.curves(Rafalt1[2880, 1437], Rafalt1, 30, closed = TRUE) : 
  Input must be a p-x-k matrix of curve coordinates

I have looked up p-x-k matrix but have not found much useful information. Can anyone tell me how a p-k-x matrix is meant to be formatted? 
I have attached an example data set. I have tried using the data as it is in the example, as well as with the specimen represented as one row with each column as an X or Y coordinate (as in define.sliders) but both have resulted in the same error message. Any help is much appreciated. 

-Ian James

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] p-x-k matrix?
parts:
Ian,

Matrices are defined by dimensions such as n x p or n x k or p x k, where the first letter is the number of rows and the last letter is the number of columns.  The “x” can be read as “by”; e.g., an n by k matrix.

For most applications in geomorph, n is the number of specimens, p is the number of points, and k the number of dimensions used for landmarks (2 or 3).

Hope that helps!
Mike
